documents.title: Rice Blast Disease: Symptoms and Identification
documents.content: Rice blast is a fungal disease that can affect rice at several growth stages, from seedlings to tillering and panicle heading. On leaves, early symptoms may appear as small bluish-green flecks that develop into spindle-shaped lesions with grey centres and dark-brown margins, particularly under moist conditions. As lesions grow and merge, leaves may dry and wither. Lesions can also occur on leaf sheaths and nodes. Node infections may girdle the stem, cause breakage, and lead to death of plant parts above the affected node. Infection near the base of the plant or panicle neck may cause white or poorly developed panicles. Neck lesions are often greyish-brown and may cause the panicle to fall over. Infection timing can affect grain formation and quality. Lesion appearance and size can vary among rice varieties.
